summary.intent: Finish work package X: fix fixed-group version alignment so a provisional bump version of an unreleased member no longer leaks into dependency range rewrites and E319 errors, then push it as a PR with checks and overlap verification.
summary.outcome: Pushed PR #580 on fix/fixed-group-final-rewrites, linked to trail #462. GAP-02 reproduced and was fixed in cascade.rs. just pre-push, lint, doc-check and test pass, commits are signed, mutants show 0 missed, and merge-tree shows no conflicts with #576 and #571.

repo: Fixed-group members that have not been released get a provisional bump version, which leaked into dependency range rewrites and E319 checks in Cargo, npm and Python. The aligned group target must be used instead.
Dependency rewrites, E319 and the dependency-update list must be derived after cascade convergence from final targets, not from intermediate ones.
If bump_target still reports a dependent as released because of the provisional version, fixing only the rewrite turns the E319 abort into a successful but wrong release.
Python and the other ecosystems should leave a satisfied range such as <=2.0.0 as written, and the dependent must not be released.
cargo mutants --in-diff output goes to mutants.out*. Do not commit these directories; mutants.out.old needs to be restored from HEAD.
Pushes use an explicit refspec (HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>), checked afterwards with git ls-remote. Overlap with other PRs is checked using git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only.
Commit signature status can be verified through gh api repos/.../commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason.
Trail linking is done with `entire trail link <n>` and `entire trail ci-pr`.

code.finding: bump_target now returns the group's aligned target for any fixed-group member, and rewrites, E319 and dependency-update listing are computed after convergence from final targets.

workflow: A fresh reviewer model caught a missed half of the bug (the dependent being released because of the provisional version), so independent review is worth running.
Mutation testing first missed 5 mutants. Adding targeted unit tests in cascade/tests.rs killed them. Black-box tests alone were not enough.
Running merge-tree against sibling PRs before pushing detects overlap early.
Work is sequenced across work packages and sessions, so a later one (K) is held until another session merges G.

friction: The first mutation run missed 5 mutants and needed extra unit tests.
The initial fix missed that the dependent was still released, which was found only at review.
just ci and just bench were not run, so coverage of the checks is partial.
